newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring wheat bids lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring wheat bids lower.

text.p: Most dark northern spring wheat bids were a bit lower Thursday, and white wheat bids were up on slow farmer sales, dealers said.
MGE July wheat settled one cent firmer at $3.83-3/4, and other months were 1/4 to 3-3/4 lower.
Several Montana grain merchandisers reported some hail on Wednesday, but they said it was too early to assess if it had done any kind of damage to the wheat.
"I'm not too sure what it did," a Montana merchandiser said. Harvesting of spring wheat should begin mid to late July, dealers said.
"The wheat looks short but stout," the merchandiser said.
The wheat was shorter than it should be due to recent cool weather, a second Montana merchandiser said.
In North Dakota, the weather was favorable and wheat stands looked good. Producers should be cutting wheat in late July and early August, a dealer said.
Regarding hard red winter wheat, clear skies through Saturday should allow the HRW wheat harvest to start in southern Kansas and advance in Oklahoma and the Texas Panhandle, U.S. meteorologists said.
